approach: Write docs/spec.toml as `[[requirement]]` and `[[question]]` tables. Each requirement has id, statement, kind, status, optional supersedes, and a `sources` list of {quote, heading}. Each question has id, text and sources. Add xtask/tests/spec.rs with a pure `check(spec_toml, brief_text) -> Result<Report, Vec<String>>` function using the toml and serde crates that xtask already lists as dev-dependencies. The real test runs it on docs/spec.toml and BRIEF.md. Whitespace-collapsed substring matching is used for quotes. In-memory negative tests cover a bad quote, a duplicate id, a missing supersedes target, and a requirement with no source. A coverage test maps each source's heading to Olympus sections 1-5 and R1-R8, and requires at least one requirement for each of those 13 groups. Then add the CHANGELOG entry, a decisions.md record (D111), and an M33 row in docs/enforcement.md so the map names the new tests. docs/ontology.toml gets a term only if one is needed (see open_questions).

decisions.choice: TOML with [[requirement]] tables, parsed with toml+serde in a Rust test
decisions.reason: The repo already uses TOML for docs/ontology.toml, and toml and serde are already xtask dev-dependencies, so nothing is hand-parsed (buy-first). Quotes can be multi-line strings. Agents and Sri can both read it.

rejected.why: It needs a hand-written parser and is easy to drift.
It has no comments, escaping long quotes is painful, and it is hard for Sri to approve by reading.
It needs a new crate, and its implicit typing and indentation rules make errors easy.

decisions.choice: Normalize both quote and BRIEF.md with `split_whitespace().join(" ")` before a substring check. Keep markdown characters in the quote.
decisions.reason: This matches the 'collapsing whitespace' criterion and lets multi-line quotes pass. 'Verbatim' stays strict apart from whitespace.

decisions.choice: Derive each source's section from its `heading` string (e.g. '1. Vision', 'R1 — Causal investigation', '3.2 …', 'Stage C — …'). The coverage test also checks that the heading text appears as a heading line in BRIEF.md, so a heading cannot be invented.
decisions.reason: The criterion counts by the sources' headings. Checking the heading against BRIEF.md keeps the count honest.

rejected.why: It duplicates the heading and can disagree with it.

decisions.choice: Coverage is limited to sections 1 to 6 now. The expected groups are listed in one const array that job two can extend.
decisions.reason: Halved scope per the user; the test must pass now.

rejected.why: It would fail until the second job.

decisions.choice: Pure `check` function that takes strings, with the negative tests built from a small valid in-memory spec mutated four ways.
decisions.reason: It shows the checker fails for each defect without touching files.

rejected.why: Extra files, and the negative cases would need tracking.

decisions.choice: Question format: `[[question]]` with id, text, and `sources` (two or more quotes). The test validates the quotes the same way, and an empty list is allowed.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for the format to be supported. The planner has not read sections 1 to 6 in full for conflicts, so the producer decides whether any exists. If none, put a top-of-file comment saying so and include one in-memory test that parses a question.

rejected.why: It would put a false claim in Sri's spec.

files.purpose: The spec for Olympus sections 1-6: requirements and questions, each with verbatim quotes and headings. It has a header comment on the format and the scope.
The `check` function, the real-file test, the four negative tests, the schema tests and the section 1-6 coverage test.
Entry for docs/spec.toml and its checking test.
Add D111: the spec format, TOML with alternatives, buy-first for toml+serde, and a note that sections 7-10, governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda come in job two.
Add a row (M33) naming the spec tests: negative `a_quote_not_in_the_brief_is_flagged`, positive `the_spec_is_valid_against_the_brief`, so M24 stays true. Test names must be defined under xtask/tests.
Only if needed. toml, serde and regex are already dev-dependencies, so likely no change. Cargo.lock then also stays unchanged.
Only if the producer finds a term in the spec that caused a misread. Per the file's own rule a term is added only when it caused a misread, so expect no change.

steps: Read BRIEF.md lines 550-865 in full. Also read the M19 and `named_tests` logic in xtask/tests/policy.rs, and the enforcement map's row format.
Write xtask/tests/spec.rs. Define serde structs for Spec, Requirement, Source and Question with `deny_unknown_fields`. Add `normalize`, `check`, the section grouping and the coverage function.
Write the negative and schema tests, starting from one valid in-memory spec and mutating it, plus a question parse test. Run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec` and see them fail on an empty spec.

Author docs/spec.toml: a header comment on the format and scope. Then requirements for sections 1-6, merged where they repeat, with statements, kinds, statuses and quotes. Add questions if the text has any, or a comment that it has none.
Run the test and fix mismatched quotes and coverage gaps until it passes.
Add the M33 row to docs/enforcement.md, D111 to docs/decisions.md and the CHANGELOG entry. Touch docs/ontology.toml only if a term caused a misread.
Run cargo fmt --all --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked. Confirm Cargo.lock needs no change.

risks.risk: Quotes with smart punctuation, tables, em dashes or markdown pipes fail to match BRIEF.md.
risks.mitigation: Copy quotes straight from the file, keep them to a sentence or a table row cell sequence, and run the test after each batch of requirements.

risks.risk: The spec file is large and takes more than one run.
risks.mitigation: Aim for one requirement per distinct idea, merge duplicates, and write a short statement. About 40 to 60 requirements is an estimate, not measured.

risks.risk: The coverage test fails on headings with em dashes or unusual spacing.
risks.mitigation: Normalize whitespace in headings, and match section groups by a prefix list: '1. Vision', '2. The Pantheon', '3', '4', '5', and 'R1' to 'R8'. Sub-headings such as '3.1' and 'Stage A' fold into their parent sections.

risks.risk: The spec could assert who runs Athena or where.
risks.mitigation: State only Olympus behavior. Run the policy test.

risks.risk: Clippy with the workspace lints rejects test code patterns.
risks.mitigation: Mirror the style of xtask/tests/policy.rs and run clippy on all targets before finishing.

demonstrations.method: Run the test that loads docs/spec.toml and BRIEF.md and runs `check`.
demonstrations.observes: `the_spec_is_valid_against_the_brief` passes. Every quote is a whitespace-collapsed substring of BRIEF.md, ids are unique, supersedes targets exist, and every requirement has at least one source.
demonstrations.fails_without: A quote not in BRIEF.md, a duplicate id, a dangling supersedes or an unsourced requirement in docs/spec.toml would make the test fail. A missing docs/spec.toml would too.

demonstrations.method: Four in-memory tests, each mutating a valid spec string, and each asserting that `check` returns an error containing a specific message.
demonstrations.observes: `a_quote_not_in_the_brief_is_flagged`, `a_duplicate_id_is_flagged`, `a_missing_supersedes_target_is_flagged` and `a_requirement_without_a_source_is_flagged` pass. A valid baseline in the same file passes `check`, so the failures come from the mutation.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `check` skipped any of the four checks, the matching negative test would see Ok and fail.

demonstrations.method: `sections_one_to_six_are_covered` groups requirements by their sources' headings and asserts a count of at least 1 for each of 13 groups: the headings of sections 1-5 and R1-R8.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. On failure it prints the groups with no requirement.
demonstrations.fails_without: If a group such as R6 had no sourced requirement, the test would fail and name it. A negative test with a spec that lacks a group asserts the coverage function reports it.

demonstrations.method: The checker also validates the schema. `kind` is one of goal, requirement, constraint, acceptance. `status` is active or superseded. The statement is non-empty and each source has a quote and a heading. The producer authors the file from sections 1-6 of BRIEF.md and merges duplicates into one requirement with several sources. Review is by reading docs/spec.toml.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes with the schema enforced. A review of the file shows requirement-bearing sentences from the Vision list, the Pantheon table, the three feedback sub-sections, Stages A-F, 5.1 and R1-R8 covered.
demonstrations.fails_without: An invalid kind or status, or an empty statement, would fail the schema check.

demonstrations.method: If a conflict or open choice exists in sections 1-6, docs/spec.toml has a `[[question]]` with both verbatim quotes. If not, a header comment says none was found, and an in-memory test shows a question with two quotes parses and one with a bad quote is flagged.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. The question quotes are validated like requirement quotes, and the question is not turned into a requirement.
demonstrations.fails_without: A question quote not in BRIEF.md would fail the check.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing policy tests, which include the M19 check that no file refers to who runs Athena or where. docs/spec.toml is a tracked file and is scanned.
demonstrations.observes: policy.rs passes. Read docs/spec.toml to confirm no statement about who runs Athena or where.
demonstrations.fails_without: A line in docs/spec.toml naming the operator or machine would trip M19, if the file is scanned.

demonstrations.method: Run cargo fmt --check, then clippy, then cargo test over the workspace. The test code uses no unwrap-style patterns that the workspace lints forbid; the producer follows xtask/tests/policy.rs style.
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0, including the M24 test that every test named in docs/enforcement.md exists.
demonstrations.fails_without: A lint, a format difference or a misnamed test in the enforcement map would fail it.

demonstrations.method: Inspect the diff of CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions.md.
demonstrations.observes: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the spec. docs/decisions.md has a new D111 stating the format, the choice of TOML with Markdown with ids, JSON and YAML as the rejected alternatives, and that sections 7-10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job.

open_questions: Whether sections 1-6 contain a conflict or open choice in Sri's words. I read only the Vision and Pantheon text (lines 550-609), not sections 3-6 in full. The producer must read all of lines 550-865 and decide.
Whether docs/spec.toml, as a tracked .toml document, is scanned by M19 for words like the operator's name. The producer should read the M19 test in xtask/tests/policy.rs first and avoid those words.
Whether `named_tests` in policy.rs reads the new enforcement row as expected, and whether `defined_tests` scans xtask/tests/spec.rs. The producer should check both before adding the M33 row.
Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock are listed as deliverables, but toml and serde already appear in xtask's dev-dependencies, so they may not change. The producer should run `cargo build --locked` to confirm.
